# Normalization {.tabset}

:BEGIN tmm
We define a normalization factor for each sample with the trimmed mean of M-values (TMM) method across all barcodes.
The assumption is that most barcodes not exhibit any differences between samples; 
any systematic differences across many barcodes are assumed to be technical and removed.

```{r}
ysub <- edgeR::normLibSizes(y)
y$samples$norm.factors <- ysub$samples$norm.factors
norm.meta <- "TMM on all barcodes"
head(y$samples)
```

The TMM normalization factors account for composition biases that are not reflected in the relative library sizes.
Specifically, composition biases are introduced when upregulation of some genes in one sample reduces the sequencing resources available for other genes.
This shifts the log-fold changes and causes spurious DE when that sample is compared to other samples with less upregulation.
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("edgeR")` handles this by computing effective library sizes (`lib.size` scaled by `norm.factors`),
which represent the combined effect of library size differences and composition biases.

```{r}
nf <- y$samples$norm.factors
names(nf) <- colnames(y)
nf <- sort(nf)
head(nf) # samples with lowest factors have more upregulated genes
tail(nf) # samples with highest factors have fewer upregulated genes
```
:END

:BEGIN lib
We perform library size normalization across all barcodes.
This assumes that any composition biases are negligible, e.g., changes in barcode abundance are more-or-less balanced in each direction.

```{r, fig.wide=TRUE}
y$samples$norm.factors <- rep(1, nrow(y$samples))
norm.meta <- "library size on all barcodes"
head(y$samples)
```
:END

We inspect the normalization results by creating MD (mean-difference) plots.
Ideally, the log-fold changes for most barcodes should be centered around zero if the normalization was successful.

```{r plot-md-norm, results="asis"}
y.cpm <- edgeR::cpm(y, log=TRUE, prior.count=3)

# Avoid creating too many plots, otherwise the compiled report is too big.
for (i in seq_len(min(9, ncol(y.cpm)))) {
    cat(paste0("\n\n## ", i, " {-}\n"))
    limma::plotMD(y.cpm, column=i)
    abline(h=0, col='red', lty=2)
}
```
